text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. The main idea is that developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Each time they do this, automated builds start automatically, so the software is always checked and ready to use. During these builds, the system runs tests to make sure everything works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines organize all these steps, from building to testing, into one smooth process. As a result, developers can fix mistakes quickly and work together more easily.
